topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students to the final lecture and introduces the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional modalities and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, detailing their mechanisms, clinical efficacy, and systemic side effects.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failure, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction, kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the inhibition of oncogenic driver kinases and explain the molecular mechanisms underpinning acquired drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies are utilized to inhibit receptor signalling, induce immune-mediated cytotoxicity, or deliver targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and evaluate clinical strategies that re-engage or engineer T cells to destroy tumors.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future directions in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the overarching obstacles in cancer management, historical improvements in patient survival, and emerging directions for future clinical practice.

topics.label: Closing case study on childhood leukemia and course conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the course with a case study on pediatric leukemia survival to illustrate the clinical realities and ethical dilemmas of cancer treatment.
